The House That Shrank Falling home prices, heavy debt, and what China, Japan and Taiwan can teach us, in eight graphic pages. 縮水的房子：房價下跌、沉重的債務，以及中國、日本和台灣能教我們的事，分成八個圖解頁面。
Shanghai, tonight01 / 08

The flat that shrank.縮水的房子

Same rooms, same view, same monthly payment. Only the price went down.一樣的房間、一樣的景色、一樣的月付金，只有房價往下掉。

Shanghai · tonight
Home prices, compared with a year earlier房價，與一年前相比
+2.8%

prices of new flats in Shanghai (September 2026)上海新建住宅的價格（2026 年 9 月）

−7.4%

prices of second-hand homes in China’s four biggest cities, Shanghai among them (March 2026)中國四大一線城市（包括上海）的二手房價格（2026 年 3 月）

For twenty years, buying a flat in China felt like a sure thing. Prices went up almost every year. Then, in 2021, they turned. New homes in China’s 70 biggest cities have now been cheaper than a year earlier for 39 months in a row.二十年來，在中國買房像是穩賺不賠：房價幾乎年年上漲。直到 2021 年，情勢反轉。中國 70 個大中城市的新房價格，已經連續 39 個月比一年前便宜。

Shanghai looks like the exception: its new flats still cost more each year. But most families don’t buy new. The homes they already own are worth less, even in the richest cities.上海看起來是例外：新房依然年年漲。但大多數家庭不是買新房，他們手上已經擁有的房子正在貶值，就連最富有的城市也一樣。

In a homeowner’s words

“I used to think housing prices … would always go up.”「我以前以為房價……會一直漲。」

Jiang, a homeowner, to the South China Morning Post, 2024一位姓江的屋主，接受《南華早報》訪問，2024 年

Your thoughts?

Have you ever bought something that lost value soon after you took it home? How did it feel?妳有沒有買過什麼東西，帶回家不久就貶值了？那是什麼感覺？

Where the money lives02 / 08

Where the money lives.錢都住在哪裡

For most Chinese families, savings have one address: home.對大多數中國家庭來說，積蓄只有一個地址：家。

Out of every 100 yuan a Chinese family owns中國家庭每擁有 100 元人民幣
70%

is in property: about 70 of every 100 yuan放在房地產裡：每 100 元人民幣約有 70 元

home and property everything else (bank savings, stocks, cash) · one symbol = 1 yuan of every 100. An estimate quoted by several research firms.房子圖示＝房地產；硬幣＝其他資產（存款、股票、現金）。每個圖示代表每 100 元人民幣中的 1 元。此為多家研究機構引用的估計值。

of Chinese households own at least one home的中國家庭至少擁有一間房子

1in 3

own two or more擁有兩間以上

Many families saw a flat as the safest savings account they could have. Parents helped their children buy one before a wedding. Some bought a second or a third.許多家庭把房子當成最安全的存錢方式。父母會在孩子結婚前幫忙買房，也有人買了第二間、第三間。

So when home prices fall, families don’t just lose money “on paper.” They feel poorer, and they start to spend less. Keep that in mind: it matters on page 5.所以房價下跌時，家庭損失的不只是「帳面上」的錢。他們會覺得自己變窮，開始減少花費。請記住這一點，第 5 頁會用到。

Your thoughts?

Where do families you know keep their savings: in a home, a bank, or the stock market? Why there?妳認識的家庭，積蓄放在哪裡：房子、銀行，還是股市？為什麼？

Twenty years, round trip03 / 08

Twenty years, round trip.二十年，繞了一圈

Up for fifteen years, down for five. After inflation, back below where it started.漲了十五年，跌了五年。扣掉通膨後，比起點還低。

After inflation, a Chinese home is worth less than in 2006扣除通膨後，中國的房子比 2006 年還不值錢

the price tag after inflation · Index, 2010 = 100 (Bank for International Settlements, via the St. Louis Fed). Lines join three points: 2006, the 2021 peak and early 2026. The real path had bumps.實線：標價；虛線：扣除通膨後。指數以 2010 年＝100（國際清算銀行，經聖路易聯準銀行整理）。線條只連接三個點：2006 年、2021 年高峰、2026 年初；實際走勢有起伏。

Why it turned為什麼會反轉
  1. 1

    Too many homes. Builders kept building, even in small cities with fewer buyers.房子太多：建商不停蓋，連買家變少的小城市也一樣。

  2. 2

    Builders in debt. In 2020 Beijing set “three red lines” on how much developers could borrow. Evergrande, the biggest, broke all three.建商負債累累：2020 年北京對建商借錢設下「三道紅線」，最大的恆大三條全踩。

  3. 3

    Fewer people. China’s population has been shrinking since 2022.人口變少：中國人口從 2022 年開始減少。

  4. 4

    Buyers wait. If prices will be lower next year, why buy now?買家觀望：如果明年更便宜，為什麼現在買？

Your thoughts?

Reason 4 feeds itself: the more people wait, the more prices fall. Have you ever waited for a price to drop?第 4 個原因會自我強化：越多人觀望，價格就跌得越多。妳有沒有等過什麼東西降價？

The math04 / 08

Your share shrinks faster.妳的那一份，縮得更快

The price falls 30%. The loan doesn’t fall at all. Guess who takes the hit.房價跌了三成，貸款卻一毛也沒少。猜猜誰吃下了損失？

the bank’s loan the part you own · All amounts in Chinese yuan (M = million). You paid 1 million and borrowed 2 million. The bank is still owed 2 million, so the whole drop comes out of your part.藍色：銀行貸款；橘色：妳擁有的部分。金額皆為人民幣（M＝百萬）。妳付了 100 萬、借了 200 萬。銀行的 200 萬一毛不少，所以下跌的部分全由妳承擔。

−30%

the price of the flat房子的價格

−90%

the part that is yours屬於妳的那一部分

This is leverage, and it cuts both ways. If the same flat had risen 30%, your part would have grown from 1 million yuan to 1.9 million. That is why borrowing to buy felt so smart for so long.這就是槓桿，而且是雙面刃。如果同一間房漲了三成，妳的那一份會從 100 萬變成 190 萬。這就是為什麼借錢買房，長久以來看起來那麼聰明。

Fall far enough and your part drops below zero. Then you owe the bank more than the flat is worth.跌得夠深，妳的那一份就會變成負數：妳欠銀行的錢，比房子本身還值錢。

The other side of the price tag

Falling prices are good news for some people. Renters, savers and first-time buyers can now get more home for less money.房價下跌，對某些人是好消息。租屋族、存錢的人和首購族，現在可以用更少的錢買到更多的房子。

Your thoughts?

Borrow and own, or rent and save? Which feels safer to you, and why?借錢買房，還是租屋存錢？哪一個讓妳覺得比較安全？為什麼？

The spiral05 / 08

The spiral, and the fix.螺旋，以及解方

When one family cuts back, it’s careful. When millions do, it’s a spiral.一個家庭縮減開支，叫謹慎；幾百萬個家庭一起縮，就成了螺旋。

37%

China’s early-repayment rate on mortgages in April 2024, a record, as families rushed to pay off loans early2024 年 4 月中國房貸的提前還款率，創下紀錄：家庭爭相提早還清貸款

The more the debtors pay, the more they owe.Irving Fisher, economist, 1933債務人還得越多，欠得越多。——經濟學家費雪，1933 年

What’s being tried正在嘗試的做法

  • Cheaper loans: mortgage rates cut, and the national lowest rate scrapped更便宜的貸款：調降房貸利率，取消全國利率下限
  • Smaller down payments: as low as 15% of the price更低的頭期款：最低只要房價的 15%
  • Fewer limits on who can buy, even in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen放寬購屋限制，連北京、上海、深圳也鬆綁
  • State firms buying empty homes to rent out cheaply, with 300 billion yuan from the central bank (2024)國營企業收購空屋轉作平價住宅，央行提供 3,000 億人民幣（2024 年）
  • Trade-in deals: swap your old flat for a new one以舊換新：用舊房換新房

The doubt: cheap loans don’t help much if people don’t want to buy.質疑的聲音：如果大家根本不想買，便宜的貸款也幫不了太多。

Your thoughts?

Paying off debt is a wise choice for one family. Why can it hurt when everyone does it at once?對一個家庭來說，還清債務是明智的選擇。為什麼大家同時這麼做，反而會造成傷害？

Tokyo, 199106 / 08

Japan did it first.日本先走過這條路

A bubble, a burst, and land prices that fell for most of a working life.一場泡沫、一次破裂，還有幾乎跌了大半輩子的地價。

Tokyo · 1991 Tokyo · 2005
Average home land prices fell every year from 1992 to 2020全國住宅地價從 1992 到 2020 年年年下跌
1992200020102020

One square = one year of falling prices, Japan’s nationwide survey of residential land. 2020 was the 29th fall in a row.一格代表一年的下跌（日本全國住宅地價調查）。2020 年是連續第 29 年下跌。

+128% → −70%

Shop and office land in Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya more than doubled from 1980 to 1991, then lost 70% by 2005, ending below its 1980 price.東京、大阪、名古屋的商業用地，1980 到 1991 年漲了一倍多，到 2005 年又跌掉七成，比 1980 年還便宜。

Zombies

Why so long? Banks kept lending to companies that could never pay them back, instead of admitting the losses.為什麼拖這麼久？銀行不肯認列損失，持續借錢給永遠還不起的企業，也就是所謂的「殭屍企業」。

How it ended

Tokyo came back. New flats in its six central wards averaged 195 million yen in 2025, close to the 1990 record of 227 million yen. Many rural towns never did.東京回來了：2025 年市中心六區的新建公寓平均 1 億 9,500 萬日圓，逼近 1990 年 2 億 2,700 萬日圓的紀錄。但許多鄉下小鎮再也沒有回來。

Your thoughts?

Imagine your home losing value almost every year for most of your working life. Would you keep it, sell it, or rent it out?想像妳的房子在妳大半輩子的職涯裡幾乎年年貶值。妳會留著、賣掉，還是出租？

Taiwan became a “super-aged” society in 2025. Only 107,812 babies were born that year, a record low.台灣在 2025 年成為「超高齡社會」。那一年只有 107,812 名新生兒，創歷史新低。

1 flat = 15 years of our pay?
Your thoughts?

Will fewer people mean cheaper homes for the young? Fewer buyers could cool prices. But Japan shows demand piles into big cities, and with fewer children per family, many young people will inherit a home while others won’t. Which side do you believe?人口變少，年輕人就買得起房子了嗎？買家少了，房價可能降溫。但日本的例子顯示，需求會集中到大城市；而且每個家庭的孩子變少，很多年輕人會繼承房子，另一些人卻不會。妳比較相信哪一邊？

Before you buy08 / 08

What “safe” really means.「安全」到底是什麼意思

A house is a real thing. That doesn’t make it a safe bet.房子是看得見、摸得到的東西，但這不代表它穩賺不賠。

When prices fall當價格下跌時

The saver

Cash buys more home each year. Waiting costs nothing, and a cheaper home may come along.同樣的存款，一年比一年買得到更多房子。等待不用付出代價，說不定還能等到更便宜的房子。

The borrower

The loan stays the same size while the home shrinks. Each payment buys less of a home.房子縮水，貸款卻一樣大。每一期還款換到的房子越來越少。

Three questions to ask about anything you call “safe”面對任何「安全」的東西，先問三個問題
  1. What do I owe?

    Debt doesn’t shrink when prices do.我欠了多少？價格縮水，債務不會跟著縮。

  2. What stays scarce?

    Machines keep making many things cheaper. Land where people want to live stays scarce.什麼東西會一直稀少？機器讓很多東西越來越便宜，但大家想住的地方，土地始終稀少。

  3. Who will still want it?

    A home is worth what the next buyer will pay. Fewer buyers, lower prices.以後還有誰會想要？房子的價值取決於下一個買家願意出多少錢。買家越少，價格越低。

A note from LENSLENS 的提醒

This issue is a discussion of economic ideas, not financial advice. Everyone’s money, family and city are different. Before a big decision, talk to a licensed professional.本期內容是經濟觀念的討論，不是理財建議。每個人的財務、家庭和城市狀況都不同。做重大決定前，請諮詢合格的專業人士。

Your thoughts?

Your parents probably said “buy a home, it’s the safest thing.” Would you say the same to your own children?妳的父母大概說過「買房子最保險」。妳會對自己的孩子說一樣的話嗎？

Before you goLENS · 02

Things to ponder.值得想一想的事

Over a cup of tea, on your own or with someone who disagrees.泡杯茶，自己想想，或找個意見不同的人聊聊。

  1. Is a home a place to live, a savings account, or both? What happens when those two jobs pull in different directions?房子是住的地方、存錢的工具，還是兩者都是？當這兩個角色互相拉扯時，會發生什麼事？

  2. Falling prices hurt owners and help first-time buyers. Should a government try to stop them? Who should it protect?房價下跌傷害屋主，卻幫了首購族。政府應該出手阻止嗎？應該保護誰？

  3. Japan’s banks hid their losses for years. Why might it be hard for anyone, a bank or a person, to admit a loss?日本的銀行把損失藏了好幾年。為什麼不管是銀行還是個人，都很難承認自己虧損？

  4. Tokyo bounced back; many small towns didn’t. Where in Taiwan do you think prices would hold up, and where wouldn’t they?東京反彈了，許多小鎮卻沒有。妳覺得台灣哪些地方的房價撐得住，哪些地方撐不住？

  5. If you inherited a flat one day, would you live in it, rent it out, or sell it?如果有一天妳繼承了一間房子，妳會自己住、出租，還是賣掉？

  6. What does “safe” mean to you: owning things, having savings, or having skills no one can take away?對妳來說，「安全」是什麼：擁有東西、有存款，還是擁有別人拿不走的能力？
